text:
Maya: Quick sync — post-launch customer asks from Acme & BetaCorp. Acme is threatening to delay renewal unless we ship two quick wins and fix a streaming edgecase. We need to decide what goes into the next 2 sprints (bugs vs enhancements) and assign owners.

Jon: Can we make a short rubric: what counts as a blocking bug vs a quick-win enhancement? I want owners + timeboxes before we commit.

Alex: From CS the priorities are small:
- stream dropout on long responses (happens ~1-2% on dedicated capacity) — reported by Acme — high
- prompt truncation when >2048 tokens (BetaCorp) — medium
- embeddings page label confusion (small UI copy) — low

Sasha: We should also consider Dedicated SLA impact — if stream dropout spikes we need a hotfix path on infra. Suggest reserving 1 eng for hotfix rotation next week.

Liam: Proposal: Sprint A (3 working days): dedicate 3 dev-days for hotfixes + 2 dev-days for UI quick wins. Sprint B (next 2 weeks): enhancements and follow-on items. If a reported customer bug meets "regression or customer blocker" criteria, it pre-empts Sprint B.

Maya: Love that. Let's formalize acceptance criteria + owners. Quick draft checklist — tag owners and timeboxes: 
```
- [ ] Stream dropout fix — owner: Alex — estimate: 3d — type: bug — rollout: canary -> regional -> global
- [ ] Prompt truncation mitigation — owner: Jon — estimate: 4d — type: bug/enhancement (prompt handling) — mitigation: UI token warning + backend fix
- [ ] Embeddings UI label — owner: Sasha — estimate: 1d — type: enhancement — release: patch next deploy
```

Jon: I can take prompt handling. I'll add a fallback to reject >8k tokens server-side and show clear error in the SDK + Console. :thumbsup:

Alex: I'll triage stream logs tomorrow and create a minimal reproducer. If we can root cause in infra path, we should do a canary patch.

Sasha: I'll ship the UI label fix and a tiny copy update. Will also update the docs page.

Maya: Please add the label `postlaunch-commit` and tag affected customer threads (Acme, BetaCorp) in the ticket. We need one shared board for visibility.

Liam: From a release gating POV: if stream error rate >0.5% after canary, we roll back and escalate to oncall. Otherwise proceed to regional.

Maya: OK — owners: Alex, Jon, Sasha. Timeboxes: 3d/4d/1d. Can each of you create a ticket with the label and estimated completion date by EOD?

Alex: Will create ticket and attach logs.

Jon: Ticket + SDK error PR coming from me.

Sasha: PR for UI copy in progress.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: 1749123605 — will report health metrics.

Maya: Thanks team. After quick wins land, let's run a 1-hour customer demo with Acme to ensure confidence for renewal. I'll schedule once deploy-bot reports green.

Jon: One more ask — can we include a small acceptance test for streaming stability in the CI? Even a smoke test would help catch regressions.

Alex: Agree. I'll add a lightweight client test that simulates long responses and asserts no 5xx or connection close within X seconds.

Maya: Perfect. That's the plan. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10am to review tickets and canary metrics. :calendar:
